findings.claim: Q2 2026 adjusted operating earnings were USD 2.55 per share against USD 1.91 a year earlier, up 33%, driven by the addition of Calpine, higher PJM capacity prices and stronger realised customer margins in the commercial business.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Full-year 2026 adjusted operating earnings guidance was raised to USD 11.50-12.50 per share from USD 11.00-12.00, reflecting strong year-to-date performance.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE

findings.claim: At USD 283.78 and a guidance midpoint of USD 12.00, the stock trades at approximately 23.6x FY2026 adjusted operating earnings — a multiple that does not depend on the uncertain share count.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Demand for the product is structurally scarce and growing, but the contracted share is what matters: 920 MW signed in one quarter at 18.5 years brings roughly 30% of clean baseload under contract.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Demand classification: the contracted ~30% of baseload at 18.5-year duration is [Existing Contracted]; the Calpine dispatchable fleet and retail book are [Existing Contracted] but short-dated; further hyperscaler PPAs are [Approved / Committed Pipeline] given the demonstrated signing rate; and the assumption that the remaining ~70% of baseload eventually contracts at similar premiums is [Speculative Demand] earning zero base-case weight.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Growth is margin-accretive at present, but the drivers are mixed in quality: Calpine is an acquisition, higher PJM capacity prices are an auction outcome, and higher realised customer margins are a commercial achievement. Only the third is repeatable by management action.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the disclosed Q2 drivers

findings.claim: The market has already substantially repriced this story. At USD 283.78 the stock is roughly 31% below its 52-week high of USD 412.70 and 24% above its low of USD 228.63 — a very different starting point from the other AI-power names in this batch.
findings.label: FACT

risks.text: Roughly 70% of clean baseload is merchant, so most of the fleet is exposed to power prices and capacity auctions rather than to the contracted premium.
Two of the three cited Q2 earnings drivers — Calpine and PJM capacity prices — are not repeatable management actions.
There is no disclosed price premium, only disclosed duration and volume. The core thesis claim is unmeasured.

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results and further PPA announcements

conclusions: Operating momentum is strong: Q2 adjusted operating EPS up 33% to USD 2.55, with FY2026 guidance raised to USD 11.50-12.50.
At USD 283.78 the stock trades at approximately 23.6x the guidance midpoint — a multiple that does not depend on the uncertain share count, and the most reliable valuation anchor in this dossier.
The demand classification is unusually favourable for this protocol. Most revenue is contracted or operating; only the extension of the premium to the remaining 70% of baseload is speculative.
The quality of the earnings drivers is mixed. Calpine is an acquisition and higher PJM capacity prices are an auction outcome; only improved customer margins are a repeatable commercial achievement.
The market has already repriced this substantially — 31% below the 52-week high. That is a materially better starting point than GE Vernova in the same batch.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 establishes that the operating case is sound and already partly in the price. Unlike the other AI-power names in this batch, a significant de-rating has already occurred, which changes the risk-reward without changing the business.
